1. __Join the dwellings_neighborhoods_ml.csv data to the dwelling_ml.csv on the parcel column to create a new dataset. Duplicate the code for the model you recommended in the previous taskn above and update it to use this data. Explain the differences and if this changes the model you recomend to the Client.__

_In efforts to keep the model as similar as the original model, the only changes made to this new model was the data, and later the features. When performing the exact same machine learning model (Random Forest) the accuracy actually fell by 0.8%. However, after including all the features from dwellings\_neighborhoods the accuracy rose by 1.1%. The charts below show a plethora of metrics but the most important may be the accuracy, precision, and recall. Notice how when we join the dataframes the metrics drop by a tiny amount, but after adding all of the features from dwellings\_neighborhoods it jumps a bit higher than the original._
_It would not be recommended to change models, as the metrics have not fallen very far, but in fact improved a bit. Recall Unit 4's task 3. It was found that Random Forest was the most effective model for the original data set. Seeing the improvements new features add, Random Forest is likely still the best model for this addition._

```{python}
#this code is so bad i am sorry
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report
from sklearn.inspection import permutation_importance
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore', category=UserWarning)

def prenteval(y_true, y_pred, label=""):
    print(f"{label} \n{classification_report(y_true, y_pred)}")
def runmymodelbleareghdfa(data, featuress, label=""):
    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
      data.select(featuress),
      data["before1980"],
      test_size=0.09,
      random_state=0
    )
    model = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100,max_depth=15,random_state=0)
    model.fit(X_train, y_train)
    y_hat = model.predict(X_test)
    prenteval(y_test, y_hat, label)

features = ["arcstyle_ONE-STORY","gartype_Att","quality_C","livearea","finbsmnt","numbaths"]
bdf = df.join(
    adf,
    on="parcel",
    how="inner"
)
runmymodelbleareghdfa(df,features,"1. Original df (6 features):")
runmymodelbleareghdfa(bdf,features,"2. Joined df (6 features):")
features += [col for col in adf.columns if col != "parcel"]
runmymodelbleareghdfa(bdf,features,"3. Joined df (+ neighborhoods):")
```
